chunks: And everything in it that is from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, I have narrated it from my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them both - Allah be pleased with them both - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi. And I have narrated it also from my father, and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with them both - from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi.

key_terms.أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْبَ: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, a prominent Shia scholar and narrator
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them both, a formula of respect for the two narrators
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I have narrated it, indicating the author's direct transmission
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ السَّعْدَابَادِ: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, a narrator in the second chain

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi's narrations verified in this text?
ai.summary: This introductory note establishes the reliability of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi’s narrations by detailing two distinct transmission chains (isnad) within Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. By citing his father and prominent companions like Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, al-Saduq underscores the scholarly rigor and authenticity of the hadith corpus, ensuring the reader of its direct lineage to the Imams.
